english: The hero lies on the ground. Now his brother has come and sat down. Now he spoke: 'Brother, I am dying. Now my fame will live. Let (him) take my spear and not weep.' Now sleep seized him, and he became famous.
uncertain: sléh₂gʷtu and HréwdHt are 3sg (imperative / injunctive) inside an address to the brother; read as 'let him take', but 2sg 'take my spear, do not weep' is surely meant
supnós 'sleep' as a death euphemism

english: Three men went to the sea. Now the broad [sea] grew dark. Now the first spoke: 'Comrades, do not tremble. Let us go over the sea and seek fame.' Now they set out. Now it swallowed them, and their fame is imperishable.
uncertain: h₁íd h₁wr̥Hú: neuter 'it, the broad one' taken as the sea (móri n.)
litént 'went away' read as 'set out'
h₁éyomes indicative beside subjunctive h₂isḱṓmes; both read as hortative

english: The father spoke to his son: 'Let (him) hear my words. Do not deceive your guest, and do not flee from the spear. Whatever you do here, your fame will be great.' Now let him go, and may the gods guard you. Now he heard the words and went away.
uncertain: ḱléwsetu (IMP.3SG), dʰrugʰyét and bʰéwgt (3sg injunctive), h₁éytu (IMP.3SG) all sit in a 2sg address with téwe/twé; read literally as 3sg
h₁yód ḱód 'what here / whatever this' construction
subject of the last sentence assumed to be the son

english: The king gave the hero a gift. 'Now I will bring you the wolf's head.' Now night came on. Now the wolf heard him and ran at him. Now he seized the wolf and split its head. Now he carried the head to the king. Now he said: 'Your name is famous.'
uncertain: speaker of the second sentence (no verb of saying; assumed the hero)
h₁nédʰt glossed 'come forth' with nókʷtm̥ accusative: 'night came' expects nominative nókʷts; possibly 'he reached the night'
speaker of the last sentence assumed the king

english: A strong man stood at the door of the house. Now he shouted: 'Whoever comes to this door will see my spear.' Now a hero of good fame came. Now he said: 'Let him go away from the door, or I will break it.' Now the strong man did not stand aside. Now he threw his spear, and the strong man fell. Now he broke it [the door] and entered the house.
uncertain: dʰurés taken as ablative 'from the door'
léyttu 3sg 'let him leave', possibly meant as 2sg to the strong man
who throws the spear (the hero, swóm)

english: The two met. 'Now who are you? I do not know you.' Now that one said: 'Your father was a guest-friend in my father's house.' Now this one said: 'Now you are my guest, and I will not kill you. Let (him) set down your spear, and let us give gifts. Let (him) take my horses and I will take your spear.' Now the two exchanged gifts and became famous.
uncertain: h₁r̥tā́m read as 3du aorist 'they two arrived/met'
dʰéh₁tu and sléh₂gʷtu are IMP.3SG in a 2sg address; 2sg 'put down your spear / take my horses' surely meant
h₁opéyetām 'made reach' = exchanged
